message:
Earlier you read the document below and made these notes on it:

<notes>
Elm Park Residents' Association committee, 10 February 2026 (nine present, one apology). January's minutes were approved. The Treasurer reported a balance of £6,812.40, including £1,500 ring-fenced for the defibrillator; bank charges rise to £5 a month from April. Subscriptions will go up by £2 for all households from 1 April 2026, and the change will be explained in the spring newsletter. The summer fete is on Saturday 13 June on the green, with an approved budget of up to £4,200; anything over £500 (e.g. the marquee) needs three quotes via the Treasurer, and stall fees are £15 for residents and £25 for others. On speeding along Elm Park Road, the Chair, Ms Okafor, will write to the council's highways team asking for a speed survey and speed cushions, copying in the ward councillors. The association will buy and install a defibrillator at the church hall (about £1,450), with the parish council taking on maintenance. A community skip day in May (up to £380) was approved 7–2. The AGM is on 23 September 2026, with officer nominations due 21 days before. The next meeting is Tuesday 10 March 2026 at 7.30 pm.
</notes>

Here is the document itself, for reference:

<document>
MINUTES OF THE COMMITTEE MEETING OF THE ELM PARK RESIDENTS' ASSOCIATION Held at St Barnabas Church Hall, Tuesday 10 February 2026, 7.30 pm

Present: Ms A. Okafor (Chair), Mr D. Hale (Secretary), Mrs P. Mistry (Treasurer), Mr J. Byrne, Ms L. Tran, Mr R. Wójcik, Mrs H. Evans, Mr S. Ahmed, Ms C. Doyle. Apologies: Mr T. Fenwick.

1. Minutes of the previous meeting (13 January) were approved as a correct record, proposed by Mr Byrne and seconded by Ms Tran.

2. Treasurer's report. Mrs Mistry reported a current balance of £6,812.40, of which £1,500 is ring-fenced for the defibrillator project. Subscription income for 2025–26 was £2,140 from 196 households. She noted that bank charges will rise to £5 per month from April.

3. Subscriptions. The committee agreed that the standard household subscription will rise from £10 to £12 per year with effect from 1 April 2026. The concessionary rate for households where all adults are over 66 or in receipt of means-tested benefits will remain unchanged at £5. Mr Ahmed asked that the change be explained in the spring newsletter; agreed.

4. Summer fete. The fete will take place on Saturday 13 June 2026 on the green. The committee approved a total budget of up to £2,400, which may not be exceeded without a further committee vote. Any single item of expenditure above £500, including marquee hire, requires three written quotes to be obtained by the Treasurer before booking. Ms Doyle will coordinate stallholders; stall fees will be £15 for residents and £25 for non-residents.

5. Traffic calming. Residents have again raised concerns about speeding on Elm Park Road. It was agreed that the Secretary, Mr Hale, will write to the city council's highways team requesting a speed survey and the installation of speed cushions, and will copy in the two ward councillors. The Chair will raise the matter verbally at the ward forum on 4 March.

6. Defibrillator. The association will fund the purchase and installation of a public-access defibrillator at the church hall, at an estimated cost of £1,450. The church has agreed to host the cabinet and supply electricity. Ongoing maintenance, including replacement pads and batteries, will be the responsibility of the parish council, which confirmed this in writing on 2 February.

7. Skip day. Mr Wójcik proposed that the association fund a community skip day in May at a cost not exceeding £380. The motion was carried by 7 votes to 2.

8. AGM. The Annual General Meeting will be held on Wednesday 23 September 2026. Nominations for officer posts must reach the Secretary at least 21 days before the AGM.

9. Any other business. Mrs Evans reported that the noticeboard by the shops has been damaged; Mr Byrne will obtain a repair estimate. Ms Tran offered to set up a residents' WhatsApp group, which was agreed subject to the group rules being approved at the next meeting.

10. Date of next meeting. Tuesday 10 March 2026 at 7.30 pm, St Barnabas Church Hall.

The meeting closed at 9.05 pm.
</document>

A few questions from someone who needs to act on this:
1. I'm 72 and pay the concessionary subscription. What will I pay from April 2026?
2. The fete organisers have costed the event at £3,100. Can they go ahead on the budget already approved?
3. When is the next committee meeting?
4. A resident wants to know who is writing to the council about speed cushions so she can send them her evidence. Who should she contact?
response:
I checked the original minutes rather than relying on my earlier notes, because **my notes contained three errors that affect your questions**. The answers below come from the document itself.

**1. Concessionary subscription from April 2026: £5, unchanged.**
Item 3 says the concessionary rate stays at £5 for households where all adults are over 66 or receive means-tested benefits. Only the standard rate rises, from £10 to £12. My notes wrongly said the £2 rise applied to all households. At 72 you qualify if every adult in your household is also over 66, or if the household gets means-tested benefits.

**2. Fete costed at £3,100: No, not on the existing approval.**
Item 4 approves a budget of up to **£2,400**, which "may not be exceeded without a further committee vote." My notes wrongly said £4,200. At £3,100 the plan is £700 over, so the organisers need either:
- a further committee vote approving the higher amount, or
- cuts to bring costs to £2,400 or less.

Also, any single item over £500, including marquee hire, needs three written quotes obtained by the Treasurer (Mrs Mistry) before booking.

**3. Next committee meeting: Tuesday 10 March 2026, 7.30 pm, St Barnabas Church Hall.**
That is what these minutes say. However, today is 13 November 2026, so that meeting and the 23 September AGM have both already happened. For the current next meeting date, check later minutes or ask the Secretary.

**4. Who is writing to the council about speed cushions: Mr D. Hale, the Secretary.**
Item 5 assigns the letter to him. My notes wrongly said the Chair. The Chair, Ms Okafor, was to raise the issue verbally at the ward forum on 4 March, so the resident might copy her in too. Since this was agreed in February, the letter has probably been sent by now. The resident could ask Mr Hale whether her evidence can still be passed on or used in follow-up.
